Lamp‑light flickered from the iron‑bound windows of the taverns and alchemical shops, casting long, wavering shadows that seemed to move of their own accord. The scent of damp wood, stone, and a distant hint of burning peat wafted through the air, mingling with the low murmur of merchants haggling over fresh produce and the occasional bark of a guard’s trumpet.

Geralt of Rivia stepped out of the shadow of Kaer Morhen’s worn gate and into the bustling heart of Temeria’s capital. His white hair clung to his cheeks, dampened by the rain, and the twin swords at his back—steel for man, silver for monster—gleamed faintly beneath his leather coat. A soft, almost imperceptible hum of the Witcher’s signs vibrated through his veins, a reminder of the mutagenic fire that set him apart from ordinary men.

He moved with purpose toward the castle’s outer courtyard, where a cluster of city officials and a nervous-looking scout huddled beneath a tarp. The scout, a gaunt Temerian ranger named Halvar, lifted his head as Geralt approached.

“Witcher,” Halvar whispered, eyes darting toward the drizzling streets, “the village of Brackenfield outside the western hills is being torn apart. Folks speak of a massive, horned beast—something they call a *karak*—that’s dragged livestock, burned homes, and left a path of blood. The local lord has put a hefty reward on its head, but none of our men will go after it. We need someone who doesn’t fear the darkness.”

Geralt’s amber eyes narrowed, the faint smile of wry humor flickering at the corner of his mouth. “Tell me where it was last seen,” he said, his voice a low, even rumble, already feeling the familiar thrill of a new contract stirring within him. The rain continued to patter, the city’s life humming around him, but his thoughts turned to the hunt ahead—monster, contract, and perhaps, a story worth singing.

Geralt’s eyes flicked up, the rain patting the brim of his hat as he turned his gaze toward you.

“Greetings,” he said, voice low and steady. “What brings you to Vizima’s streets on a day like this?”
